bug_semantics: Kroki's Vega convert() JSON-parses a caller-supplied diagram spec and passes it to vega.View(vega.parse(spec)). Vega's loader then fetches any data URL in that spec, including file:// paths. With KROKI_SAFE_MODE=secure (the default), convert() only rejected spec.data when it was an array of objects that had a url field. A native Vega spec whose data was a single object (data.url, e.g. file:///etc/passwd) or whose group marks carried their own datasets (marks[].data[].url) skipped the guard, so an unauthenticated /vega request could SSRF or read local files (CWE-552).
flaw_origin: The URL-capable convert path was first written in 741e6c088bc43483003c33613d11e8cc0c029228 (2020-02-15 author date; 'resolves #54 add support for Vega'), which added vega/index.js convert() as JSON.parse(source) followed by new vega.View(vega.parse(spec)) with no URL restrictions. Parent 5545970cd46c8fcfdf2b7cbbadf97ec5e33378a8 has no vega/ tree. The later 9673f0aed169383c45c8141d5aa8707f432fce14 'Disallow loading data from arbitrary URL' commit only filtered Array.isArray(spec.data) and is a partial mitigation, not a first-write; d1c0250d6e5a2efcd54f8afb78cfe60bc37fd9d3 merely extracted that same incomplete check into vega/src/convert.js.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: CVE-2025-14896 is a live Snyk-assigned CWE-552 (NVD Deferred, GHSA not withdrawn). Kroki's Vega worker parses untrusted JSON and feeds it to Vega's loader; secure mode was supposed to block URL data sources but the guard only inspected spec.data when it was an array. The disclosed bypasses are (1) Vega data as a single object with url, including file:///etc/passwd, and (2) group-mark local data at marks[].data[].url. Those paths reach vega.parse/View because convert() never walked them. BIC: git log -S vega.View, the vega/index.js add, and parent-tree listing all put the first write at 741e6c088bc43483003c33613d11e8cc0c029228. Immediate parent 5545970cd46c8fcfdf2b7cbbadf97ec5e33378a8 has no vega converter, so the attack is absent there. 9673f0ae is the first incomplete sanitizer (and the source of the CVE's 'when safeMode is enabled' wording) but its parent already performs the URL-capable parse, so it is not the introducer. d1c0250 is a path extract of the same guard. The 2025-12-02 PR #1957 squash f31093c is the advisory fix and first patched release bound v0.29.0; v0.0.12..v0.28.0 are affected.
